dialogue.mcacapitals_petition_menu: What do you petition the sovereign for?
dialogue.mcacapitals_petition_menu.mcaca: Petition for Hand of the Crown
dialogue.mcacapitals_petition_noble_menu: What noble dignity do you seek?
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_heir_appa: Did you hear that {heir_name} was named Heir Apparent of {capital_name}? I wonder what they will be like when they take the throne.
Do you think naming {heir_name} as Heir Apparent will settle the succession?
Have you noticed how carefully people speak about {heir_name} since the Heir Apparent announcement?
I wonder how long {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} had been considering {heir_name}.
Naming {heir_name} Heir Apparent should settle things, though I doubt everyone will let it.
Have you heard whether the court expected {heir_name} to be named Heir Apparent?
Do you think {heir_name} wanted to be named Heir?
I suppose {heir_name} has fewer ordinary days ahead now.
Have you heard anyone question the choice of {heir_name} as Heir Apparent?
Do you think naming {heir_name} as Heir will quiet the court, or give it something new to whisper about?
Why does every succession decision make people suddenly pretend they understand the whole royal line?
I would not want every room watching me the way they will watch {heir_name}.
Whatever people think of the choice, {heir_name} has become impossible to ignore.
I wonder who was pleased to hear {heir_name} named, and who had to pretend.
Have you heard whether {hand_title} {hand_name} supported {heir_name} being named Heir Apparent?
I suppose {heir_name} had no choice but to accept. You do not decline an order from the Crown.
Naming an heir settles some questions and opens others. Watch the court over the next few weeks.
I wonder what {heir_name} thinks when they look at {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} now.
I do not envy {heir_name}. The title is a gift that never stops costing something.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_crown_chi: Did you hear a {heir_title} was born in {capital_name}?
Did you hear?! A {heir_title} gives {capital_name} something hopeful to gossip about.
Have you noticed how quickly people started talking about succession after the royal birth?
Why does a newborn Crown Prince or Princess become court business before they can even open their eyes?
Do you think {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} is relieved to have a crown child in the line?
I wonder if {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} has slept since the birth.
Have you heard about the newest member of the Royal family? I hope the child grows up knowing more kindness than politics.
Why does every royal cradle seem to attract a dozen political opinions? It's just a baby.
I heard the household is well, which is better news than any title.
I hope the newborn gets a quiet room before the court turns them into a symbol.
Why are people already discussing the future of a child who has barely arrived?
Imagine being so important to the royal line before you can even hold your own head up.
Do you think the court will let the royal household enjoy the birth before turning it into strategy?
Why does the birth of a Crown Prince or Princess make everyone count the royal line out loud? It's just a baby.
Have you noticed how proud people sound when they talk about the new {heir_title} of {capital_name}?
People keep debating what the child will be like. The babe is only a week old.
I went to see the baby. It looked like a baby. The whole court acted like it had invented something.
It is strange how a newborn can change the order of everything without doing a single thing.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_capital_f: They say {capital_name} has a proper sovereign now. Strange to think we were just a village not so long ago.
People keep asking me how I feel about it. Honestly? Safer. A capital needs someone at the top.
{sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} was chosen from among us. Not some faraway lord. One of our own.
I never thought I'd live in a capital. And here we are.
The herald's been announcing it all morning. {capital_name} has a sovereign. I imagine the neighbouring villages have heard of it by now.
Some folks weren't sure about the Charter. But what's the alternative? You can't just leave a village with nobody at the helm.
I thought a capital needed walls before it needed titles. Apparently not
Someone asked if the sovereign outranks the mayor but we no longer have one. We have a sovereign now, apparently.
I remember when this was just a handful of houses and a well. Look at it now.
There is a kind of pride in being here at the beginning. I will admit to that.
I've heard of capitals. Read about them, even. I never thought I'd live in one.
The neighbouring villages will hear about this by supper, if they haven’t already.
People keep calling it progress. I'm not sure what its progress toward, but I'm sure we'll find out.
They’re calling us a capital now. I still saw a pig in the well this morning.
The Charter changed the place faster than the builders ever did.
A capital, they say. Same mud, better arguments.
We needed structure. Whether we needed a throne is a different question. But here we are.
People keep saying {capital_name} feels different now. I supposed it does, but the mud is the same.
A capital, they say. Same mud, better arguments.
The square is busy today. Either the court has news, or the market has gossip.
The first morning as a capital, and the well is still where everyone gets the news.
{capital_name} has been loud all morning. I blame the court until proven otherwise.
The village felt smaller before all these titles arrived.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_royal_mar: The court gossip before the wedding was almost as good as the wedding itself.
I saw the consort at the ceremony. A proper royal household now, {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} won't be ruling alone.
{capital_name} has been talking since the wedding.
Funny how a wedding changes a person's title overnight. One day a subject, the next a consort.
The herald couldn't stop smiling when he made the announcement. You'd think he was the one getting married.
I heard the ceremony was brief. {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} doesn't seem the type for ceremony.
A royal spouse means an heir eventually. That's what everyone's really thinking about.
People keep congratulating me as if I had anything to do with the Royal Wedding. Obviously not, I just live here.
Word spreads fast in {capital_name}. The gossip had it before the herald did.
The consort stays close to {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name}, always. I'm not sure if that's affection or politics.
Someone asked about heirs before the feast was cleared. No shame in this capital.
A royal wedding gives everyone an excuse to dress better and behave worse.
I saw the newlyweds walking through {capital_name} together. They looked good together.
{capital_name} will be talking about the royal marriage until something louder happens.
I wonder if the consort knew what they were agreeing to when they accepted the proposal.
Did you hear about the Royal Wedding? I sent a gift. Nothing grand, I figured everyone else would send something grand.
They say the couple seems genuinely fond of each other. That's rarer than people admit.
Whatever people think of the match, a royal marriage is a statement. {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} is building something.
An heir becomes more likely after a royal marriage, everyone knows it. I’d bet my last emerald that the court is already planning.
The gossip about the wedding has already outlasted the wedding itself.
The wedding’s done, but the market is still talking like it just started.
I heard the vows were short. Good. Some of us have work to do.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_sovereign: The court feels hollow right now. That's the only word for it.
I've never seen so many villagers in black at the same time. The whole capital changed overnight.
Grief in a capital is never private. Somehow we all grieve together whether we want to or not.
Black cloth went up before the market even opened.
{capital_name} is {mourning_status}. Even the square knows to keep quiet.
Two days of mourning, that's the rule. It feels both too long and not long enough.
The court looks smaller today.
The court has been moving quietly since {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} died.
The mourning started before some people had even heard the news.
Someone asked about succession already. I wish I were surprised.
The dowager has my sympathy. I cannot imagine.
If you are going to the hall, speak softly today.
Already, we have a new sovereign. I can’t imagine the pain of all those who were left behind.
The mourning will end in a day or two and the court will carry on. It's for the best, I think.
Careful, people are speaking softly, but not all silence means grief.
{capital_name} is {mourning_status}. Whatever comes next, it won't be the same.
Someone asked who knew first. Strange.
The market went quiet when the herald arrived. I've never heard it like that before.
I've lived in {capital_name} long enough to see two rulers now. Every time the court shifts, the whole place shifts with it.
The dowager doesn't speak at court much. But when they do, {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} listens.
The capital is quieter than I've ever heard it. Even the market sounds muffled somehow.
I saw black cloth being carried out before the announcement.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_throne_se: Seizing the throne is one thing. Holding it is another. We'll see.
The whole thing was over in moments, but the court is still shaking.
The old royal family is gone now. Just like that. Years of court life, erased.
I won't say I'm surprised. Anyone paying attention could see how much standing they'd built up.
The commander's support made the difference, they say. Remember that the next time someone tells you the military office is just ceremonial.
I keep wondering what happens to the children. What happens to them when the dynasty falls?
The commander’s name keeps coming up after the coup. I wonder if they knew.
The old royal household passed through the square today. Nobody knew where to look.
After the throne was seized, everyone suddenly found somewhere else to be.
I moved the good crockery inside when the shouting started. Priorities.
People are choosing their words carefully since the coup.
What counts as loyalty when the person you were loyal to no longer holds the throne?
Someone asked what side I was on. I was standing near the door.
People keep asking whose side I was on. In truth, I am on the side of whoever wins.
The square emptied faster than I’ve ever seen it.
A throne seized by force will always have that fact attached to it.
People are choosing their words very carefully today.
I saw the {hand_title} change direction when they saw the guards. Do you think they knew?
Every sovereign who has ever lost a throne probably thought it couldn't happen to them.
Well, you know what they say. Fortune favors the bold.
The commander's role in all of this is going to be discussed for years.
History remembers coups differently depending on who survives to write them. I wonder who will write about this.
Nobody who was there will stop talking about it. Nobody who wasn't there will stop asking.
There are no innocent bystanders in a coup. Everyone was already taking a side; they just didn't know it.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_disinheri: I wonder what finally pushed the Crown to remove them from the line.
One moment, you are a member of the Royal Family. The next, you are simply a name the court no longer dares to say aloud.
People keep asking what happened. Nobody seems to know for certain. Or nobody's willing to say.
It shook the nobles more than anyone expected. Disinheritance reminds everyone that their standing is not guaranteed either.
Did you hear of the disinheritance? People are talking about it, but nobody's talking too loudly. You never know who's listening.
Someone loses a claim, and somehow everyone else starts standing taller.
A disinheritance changes more than one person's future. Everyone in the line moves.
I wonder whether the disinheritance protects {capital_name} or only delays trouble.
I saw a teenager mention the disinheritance by the well and then get pulled away by the sleeve.
The disinheritance came down this morning. People stopped using the name very quickly.
Families can survive many things, but public shame is a stubborn wound.
I would not want to be seated near that household at supper.
The disinheritance has the nobles whispering more than usual.
Everyone will pretend this ends the matter, which usually means it does not.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_legitimiz: Did you hear of the recent legitimization? Some of the older courtiers were not pleased. They weren't going to say that out loud, of course.
Legitimization reshapes the succession. I hope I'm not affected.
It's a kind thing, if you think about it. Giving someone a place they didn't have before.
The herald announced the legitimization this morning. You could hear the murmuring all the way to the outer buildings.
The court took the announcement of the legitimization more quietly than I expected.
Did you hear who was just legitimized? Some at court were surprised, but I think others clearly expected it.
A child recognized by the dynasty is part of the succession now. That changes things for everyone in the line.
Did you hear someone was legitimized? That changes the family record.
The royal family tree gained another branch. The Maester will need more ink.
The legitimization has the court counting heirs again.
The decree made it official, but people have been gossiping about it happening for longer.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_abdicatio: Did you hear about the abdication? I didn't think they would actually do it. But the declaration was signed, and here we are.
I always thought abdication was rare. Most people hold onto power until something takes it from them.
Did you hear the sovereign abdicated? That is a heavy choice.
The court always adjusts eventually, but it'll take time after something like this.
A sovereign who steps down is either very wise or very tired. Maybe both.
I keep hearing people ask why they abdicated the throne. I'm not sure there's ever one reason for something like that.
Did you hear of the abdication? The herald had a whole speech prepared.
There's a new ruler in {capital_name}, and the old one is still walking around. That's a strange thing to get used to.
{sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} doesn't hold court the way the last sovereign did. This one listens more.
I watched the former sovereign walk through the square afterward. They looked lighter, if anything.
Whether the decision was wise or not will depend on what the successor does with the throne.
The abdication has everyone confused about how to address the former sovereign. Should we still bow?
The former sovereign crossed the square today. Half the market nearly bowed twice.
I wonder whether stepping down felt like relief or defeat.
The former sovereign will still be watched, even without the Crown.
Do you think the old Sovereign still gets the good chair?
Some people call it weakness because they never had to rule.
The abdication has the court rearranging itself like furniture, and I'm glad to not be a part of it.
I saw someone bow to the new sovereign, then turn and bow to the old one too.
Nobody quite knew where to stand during the transition. Court etiquette doesn't cover this often enough.
The new sovereign has the throne, but the former sovereign still has the respect of half the capital.
The former sovereign still lives here. I’m not quite sure how to address them. Do I bow? I think I should bow.
I think the former sovereign is relieved. The court is the only one having trouble letting go.
A sovereign who chooses to step down before they are forced to — that takes a particular kind of person.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_new_duke_: Dukedom isn't given lightly. {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} must have seen something worth rewarding.
I knew them before the title. They were good people then. The title has not changed that yet.
The herald announced the new dukedom loud enough for the farmers the hear it in the fields.
The court loves a new title. Gives everyone something to misuse.
A petition for dukedom requires real standing. Whoever was elevated earned their way to that desk.
Did you hear? Another villager raised to Dukedom, the herald made the announcement not long ago. I could hear it from the other end of {capital_name}.
Being a Duke sounds magnificent until you realize how many people are now watching your every move.
I put in a petition once, a long time ago. Never heard back.
I've known them since before they received their title. It's strange to bow to someone you've shared meals with.
Did you hear? Someone gained a title, and half the court gained a reason to visit.
I hope the new Duke or Duchess remembers who treated them kindly before.
Someone became a Duke and immediately forgot how doors work.
If a noble asks for directions, give them the long way.
Every new noble house makes old noble houses sit straighter.
If this is about your rank, ask the court. If this is about work, ask anyone else.
The lords have been gathered near the hall. Either news or vanity.
Titles, make people visible, and visibility is not always kind.
I hope {capital_name} gained a leader, not just another rivalry.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_lord_comm: {commander_name} is Lord Commander now! I feel safer already just knowing that.
The military office isn't just ceremonial. At least not now with {commander_name} in it.
A capital without a commander is nervous. {capital_name} can relax a little now.
Lord Commander. Even the title sounds like armour.
The herald announced {commander_name}, but the barracks seemed to know first.
I spoke with one of the knights after the announcement. They seemed genuinely relieved about the new Lord Commander.
At least the appointment explains why the road patrols doubled.
The appointment required real standing to earn. You do not give that office to someone you are uncertain about, {sovereign_name} must trust them.
The Lord Commander's appointment had every guard standing straighter by noon.
Some of the guards weren't sure how to react at first. Now they seem steadier. A good commander does that.
A court with a Lord Commander is a court that can defend itself. That changes the conversation with everyone outside {capital_name}.
I feel safer knowing the military office is filled. A capital without a commander is vulnerable in ways people don't appreciate until it's too late.
The appointment wasn't surprising. They'd been building toward it for a while.
Lord Commander is a title with real weight. Not just ceremony — genuine battlefield authority.
Did you hear? We have a new Lord Commander. It took a significant petition to earn that office. The standing required isn't easy to build.
The capital feels more organized now. There's a chain of command, and everyone knows their place in it.
Did you hear {commander_name} was made Lord Commander?
I heard {commander_name} is strict, though strict may be what {capital_name} needs.
{capital_name} may sleep easier if {commander_name} proves steady.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_hand_of_t: {hand_name} is Hand now. That's real power, more than most titles in the Capital.
The new Hand speaks with {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name}'s voice when they're not here to address the Capital.
Does that mean that {hand_name} is as powerful as a King, now?
I wonder if {hand_name} knew how many complaints came with the honor.
Being Hand sounds like an honor. I think it's mostly just work.
The court feels more organized with that office of the Hand filled. There's someone to go to now.
I saw {hand_name} speaking with the herald this morning. Something's being prepared, I just don't know what.
I heard some people say {hand_name} was an odd choice for a Hand. I think they underestimated them.
The Hand's office being filled is the single best thing that could happen to this court right now.
I hope {hand_name} can say no without starting ten arguments.
I've heard them described as the sovereign's shadow. Personally, I think of them more as the sovereign's spine.
A good Hand prevents more crises than they solve. If they're good at their job you'll never notice the ones they prevent.
The herald went on at some length about the appointment. The new Hand looked mildly embarrassed by the fuss.
Being Hand means being responsible for things that go wrong when no one else claims them. A thankless job done well.
The court has someone proper to blame now that {hand_name} has the office.
Every capital needs someone willing to sort through the mess. I'm just glad it's not me.
The herald announced {hand_name}, and three people left to go bother them.
If {hand_name} is wise, they will listen before answering.
{hand_name} looked busy even before the title. Bad sign for them.
The Hand appointment has the court acting organized. For once.
The appointment required significant trust from the Sovereign. You don't give that office to someone you're unsure of.
The court feels different with a Hand in place. Steadier. Like someone finally checked that the foundation was sound.
{hand_name} is Hand now. I saw three people waiting outside their door before breakfast.
People who could not get the sovereign's attention are already lining up outside the Hand's door.
Someone brought {hand_name} a petition with soup spilled on it. I wish I were joking.
{hand_title} sounds grand until you see all the paperwork that comes with it.
The Hand’s office is full again. I'm glad, people were starting to bring their problems to the rest of us.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_grand_mae: They've been a cleric here for years. Now look at them. {grand_maester_name} is the crown’s most learned voice.
I heard that {grand_maester_name} declined a celebration. Said there was too much reading to catch up on.
{grand_maester_name} doesn't say much in public. The advice goes to {sovereign_name} privately.
Every great court has a scholar at the heart of it. {capital_name} has one now with {grand_maester_name}.
Did you hear {grand_maester_name} was appointed Grand Maester?
Whatever wisdom the court needs that isn't military — that's {grand_maester_name}'s domain now.
The new Grand Maester was a cleric before, and they've has been here longer than most. The title is overdue, if you ask me.
I spoke with the Grand Maester briefly after the ceremony. They seem unchanged by the title, so that's a good sign.
Knowledge is the only kind of power that doesn't come with enemies attached. Usually.
{grand_maester_name} is Grand Maester now. The archives finally look supervised.
{sovereign_name} has a Grand Maester. The court may get longer answers.
I hope {grand_maester_name} has patience, because this capital has plenty of fools.
I saw extra paper carried to the archives after the appointment.
A Grand Maester hears sickness, secrets, and excuses in equal measure. I certainly do not have the patience for the position.
The court has a learned voice now, but it still has to listen.
{grand_maester_name} may learn more about {capital_name} than any noble.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_royal_gua: I saw the royal guard follow {sovereign_name} through the Capital earlier today.
I heard the Royal Guards arguing over who gets to stand closest to the sovereign.
I heard the members of the Royal Guard have to follow {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} wherever they go. When do they get to sleep?
Royal guards answer only to {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name}. Nobody else gets to give them orders. Not even the Lord Commander.
If {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} dies on their watch, the Royal Guards will be disgraced. How would they survive living here, knowing that?
Did you hear someone was appointed to the royal guard? That is an honor people admire from a safe distance.
A royal guard is never just decoration, no matter how fine the armor looks.
There's a reason the guard position requires real standing to appoint. You don't put just anyone that close to a sovereign.
Someone tried to call over the Royal Guard while they were with {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name}. That went nowhere.
Did you hear about the new Royal Guards? I heard their family is proud, though pride and worry often look alike.
The appointment was short, but the guards looked like they had stopped breathing.
The old guards watched the new royal guard very closely.
The royal guard has a different walk already.
Honor has a way of arriving with a burden tucked behind it.
The royal guard carries no rank above what the sovereign gives them. But everyone gets out of their way regardless.
The selection was not announced in advance. The chosen ones found out in the hall.
I heard about the Royal Guards. Whatever they are paid, it is not enough.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_peaceful_: The petition route is harder than it looks. You don't build that kind of standing in a week.
The old sovereign stepped back graciously. I wasn't sure they would, but I was wrong about them.
The standing required to challenge a throne through petition is extraordinary. Most people never get close.
A peaceful succession means the guard does not have to choose a side, I'm sure they're grateful for it. I know I am.
The throne changed hands without anyone drawing steel. I didn't know we did that here.
The petition for the throne worked. That will make half the capital ambitious by morning.
The former sovereign stood there while the new one was named. Hard room to breathe in.
Did you hear the Crown passed peacefully? That is the kind of news people should appreciate more than they do.
{capital_name} has a new ruler, and nobody had to draw any iron to make it happen.
The former sovereign's title is gone now. Their household, too.
People said you couldn't take a throne without a fight. Those people have never been to {capital_name} before.
The herald had to announce a new ruler with the old ruler still there. I don't imagine that was comfortable for anyone.
Have you heard about the new succession? I wonder how many expected trouble and how many are pretending they did not.
I never thought I'd see a throne change hands without something being broken.
It takes an unusual kind of character to give up a throne willingly. The former sovereign has my respect.
Building that kind of standing takes years. Most people give up before they get close.
I think the former sovereign was relieved. There's a kind of weight that comes off a person when the burden passes to someone else.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_royal_bir: Did you hear there was a royal birth? I hope the new little Prince or Princess is doing well.
The herald said the name of the newest addition to the Royal Family twice. Still didn’t catch it.
A new royal child gives {capital_name} something hopeful to talk about.
I heard the baby cried through the whole announcement.
{capital_name} seems warmer when people have new life to celebrate.
Did you hear? A new royal child, and already people are counting who stands where.
I heard the baby cried louder than the herald's announcement.
Someone already started talking succession. The child’s barely here.
The royal household needed more noise, apparently.
{capital_name} has been talking about the baby all morning.
That makes {royal_child_count} royal children now, if I’ve counted right.
That baby has more titles than I have boots.
{capital_name} does love a royal birth.
People are debating whether the new child looks more like {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} or {consort_title} {consort_name}. I think they look a little like the {hand_title} -oh...
{sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} has a new child. The whole capital’s been counting fingers and titles.
The royal children are growing up in a {capital_name} that is bigger every year. They will not know the quiet version.
I heard the new baby was healthy and loud. Good lungs for a capital.
I keep track of the royal children loosely. Mostly I let the herald do it.
{sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} has a new child. Everyone has already decided who the baby looks like.
That makes {royal_child_count} royal children now. Someone check my count.
The market has been talking about the baby all morning. Nobody agrees on who it looks like.
The royal household has {royal_household_count} people in it now. No wonder the hall is always noisy.
I saw a guard carrying blankets to the royal rooms. They looked more nervous than during a raid.
I heard someone ask about succession before the child was even named. Honestly, some people have no shame.
The royal household has {royal_household_count} people now. The hall will not be quiet again.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_court_her: The new herald’s got lungs, I’ll give them that.
The new herald’s got a voice on them. I heard the appointment from inside my house.
I watched {herald_name} practice the full title list before breakfast. Honestly, I thought it was impressive.
{herald_name} announced their own appointment. Strange way to start a job, but at least they're excited.
The square has been significantly louder since {herald_name} took the office.
A capital without a herald is a capital full of rumors. We have both now, but at least one of them is official.
The herald’s office is filled now. That should keep {latest_event} from being told five different ways.
{herald_name} was named Court Herald. The square will never know peace again.
The herald appointment explains all the shouting by the well this morning.
The herald's first official announcement was flawless. They had clearly rehearsed it many times.
The well-gossipers looked offended when the new herald was announced.
The Court Herald is named. Now the news can arrive loudly instead of merely wrong.
{herald_name} has been named Court Herald. I hope they know how to pronounce all those titles.
The new herald practiced by the well this morning. Half of {capital_name} heard the warmup.
The herald’s office is filled again. Good. People were starting to invent their own announcements.
The court has a herald again. The well-gossipers looked offended.
I hope the new herald likes repeating things. People never listen the first time.
The appointment was announced loudly enough to scare the chickens.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_news_mourning_: The market is louder already after mourning. Two days of quiet was its own kind of loud.
The herald announced the end of mourning at first light. Kept it short, for once.
Two days in black felt longer than two days. I’m glad to see colour again.
The market sounded more like itself this morning. Not all the way, but closer.
People are finding their way back to ordinary life. It takes a day or two after the cloth comes off.
{herald_name} announced the end of mourning at first light. No grand speech, thankfully.
The guards look less rigid today. Mourning takes something from everyone, even them.
The first morning after mourning always feels uncertain. Then the market opens, and we begin again.
At least the square has color in it again. Still, this will take some getting used to.
It feels strange seeing the guards in regular dress again.
I suppose life moves whether hearts are ready or not. I wonder how the {sovereign_title} is feeling after everything.
The herald announced the end of mourning without making a meal of it.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_capital_topic_: People are still talking about {latest_event}. I imagine they will be for a while yet.
A capital this size generates politics whether you want it to or not. Best not to be in the middle of it.
{capital_population} people in {capital_name} now. Every day there's someone new I don't recognize.
The chronicle records more than most people realize. It's worth reading, if you get the chance.
Have you noticed how many new faces are passing through {capital_name} lately?
The road into {capital_name} has been busy all morning.
The well knows more secrets than the council at this point.
{capital_name} feels louder every season.
Someone should tell the nobles that doors are for entering, not whispering beside.
The inn has been full more often than not lately.
{capital_population} residents is a lot of mouths to feed.
Court gossip moves faster than the herald's announcements. Always has.
People carry themselves differently now that this place has status.
Some folks resent the titles. Others want one desperately. I recommend just keeping your head down.
The roads need attention before the next season turns them worse.
Every time something changes in the court, I hear about it before the morning is out. This place cannot keep a secret.
{capital_name} feels busier every time I walk through it, and I am starting to miss when I knew where everyone lived.
People are always watching the royal children, waiting to see who becomes what. What a horrible way to live.
I heard {heir_name} arguing with one of the guards. Not about anything serious, but it was strange to see the heir looking so ordinary.
The royal household has {royal_household_count} people in it now. It runs like a small village on its own.
The court keeps inventing ways to make standing in a room complicated.
When a place grows this quickly, even familiar faces start to feel like part of a crowd.
A new title always makes the square louder.
If {latest_event} involves a title, give the gossip until supper.
A larger village means more helping hands, more hungry mouths, and more people certain they know best.
If a noble asks for directions, I always give them the long way.
The old residents remember when news traveled slowly; now a whisper can cross {capital_name} before supper.
If this is about rank, ask the court. If this is about work, ask anyone else.
A place with {capital_population} residents can survive many things, but not everyone talking at once.
I do not mind growth, but I mind when growth makes neighbors forget they are neighbors.
{capital_name} is still home, even if it feels less simple than it used to.
{capital_name} has enough pride already; what it needs most is people who can be relied on.
Some days {capital_name} feels noble, and some days it feels like everyone misplaced their patience.
A good reputation takes years to build and one foolish noble to damage.
Have the roads felt busier to you lately, or have I just been noticing more strangers?
Do you think children growing up in {capital_name} will see this place differently than we do?
The fisherman said the water has been strange lately, and I do not like when fishermen start sounding thoughtful.
I passed the shepherd earlier, and the sheep were behaving better than half the people in {capital_name}.
The butcher keeps a sharper knife than tongue, which is more than can be said for most of {capital_name}.
Have you noticed the farmer watching the sky more than the fields lately?
Did the fisherman seem worried to you, or does staring at water just do that to a person?
I would not call {capital_name} quiet, but it has a way of going still when royal names are mentioned.
The children have been playing at court again. Their judgments are quicker than the real ones.
Do you ever feel like half the capital is listening even when no one is looking at you?
Do you ever wonder what travelers say about {capital_name} after they leave?
Some people want the capital to grow. Some only want it to grow around them.
Nothing reveals character like a shared shortage.
Do you think children born here will believe {capital_name} was always this important?
People talk about honor most when coin is not enough.
For all its troubles, {capital_name} is where people are trying to make tomorrow better than today.
If people still choose to raise children here, then {capital_name} must mean something worth trusting.
A capital is a proud thing, but home is what makes people defend it.
Some villagers stay for duty, some for family, and some because leaving would feel like losing part of themselves.
The Crown may rule {capital_name}, but memory is what makes people belong to it.
The future is easy to praise when you are not the child expected to live in it.
Every family here is betting, in its own quiet way, that {capital_name} will be worth staying for.
People speak of legacy like it belongs to rulers, but ordinary families leave one too.
The children in {capital_name} will grow up thinking crowns and titles are ordinary things.
I wonder what the young ones will remember most about this place when they are grown.
The future of {capital_name} may depend less on decrees and more on what the children learn watching us.
It is strange to think the children playing today may be the ones holding {capital_name} together later.
…I only said it once, and now half the square has an opinion.
Someone keeps feeding the cats near the square. Now the cats hold court there.
…that is not what I said. That is what they heard. There is a difference.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_commoner_: People used to gossip about trades. Now it’s titles.
Every villager in {capital_name} has an opinion now.
The herald’s been busy since {latest_event}.
I heard a noble complain about hard work today, and I nearly laughed.
Someone asked me if I’d ever petition for a title. I said I like sleeping.
I know enough about court business to avoid court business.
If the sovereign wants my opinion, I’ll be in the field.
Us commoners know the state of {capital_name} by the mud on our boots.
The children of {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} will inherit a different {capital_name} than the one that was chartered. Whether that's better or worse is yet to be seen.
I think {heir_title} {heir_name} will be a good ruler someday. They ask more questions than most people expect an heir to ask.
The worst part of being a Capital is that people with rank speak of duty, but ordinary folk like me carry most of it home.
{sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} seems like a fair ruler so far, but we’ll see how that holds.
I couldn't tell you the full succession order, but I know {heir_title} {heir_name} is next in line. Everyone knows that much.
I used to know everyone here. Now I know everyone’s title instead.
Someone asked me who I support. I said the person paying fair for wheat.
I do not mind the court, so long as it stays far away from me.
A guard told me to clear the road. I was already clearing it.
The nobles talk like the rest of us do not have ears.
I know enough about succession to know I want no part of it.
The capital got bigger. My house did not.
If the herald wants me, they can shout. They usually do.
Honestly, if the Crown wants to know the truth about {capital_name}, it should ask whoever stands in the bread line.
People ask me if I'd ever petition for a title. I don't have the standing. Or, frankly, the patience.
We commoners notice everything because no one bothers hiding things from us.
The latest news — {latest_event} — hasn't changed my daily life much. But the court seems to think it matters enormously.
I don't follow politics. Politics follows me. That's what living in a capital teaches you.
I couldn't tell you the full title hierarchy if you paid me 50 emeralds. I know who matters, though.
I saw the royal guard pass through the market today. Impressive. Also a little unsettling.
{capital_name} only stands because people without titles keep showing up.
People keep asking if I want to petition for something. I want to live quietly and not be noticed, that's my only petition.
If work earned rank, half the square would be royal by now, but sure, give the gentleman with a title a grant.
I think the sovereign is doing well. I base that on almost no information and a general feeling. I think that's how most people do it.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_01: Sir is a title. The sword work behind it is what actually matters.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_02: I heard someone call guard duty exciting. They have clearly never stood watch in bad weather.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_03: A knight without discipline is just a soldier with a fancier name.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_04: My position allows me to visit every building in the Capital. I know every road in and out of {capital_name}, and everyone in it.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_05: I was knighted in {capital_name}. This is my home, and I will defend it as such.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_06: People think the knightly rank is ceremonial. Come stand watch when a Pillager raid finds their way to the Capital.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_07: Sir. Dame. The title marks what we do and who we serve. I think that is as it should be.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_08: The regular knights respect the Royal Guard. Most of them, anyway. The ones who don't learn quickly.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_09: I have stood through mourning, through celebration, through raids. The guard does not stop for any of it.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_10: This is the most important role I will ever hold in {capital_name}. I intend to hold it without fault.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_11: The knightly rank means I am part of this court's defence in a way that goes beyond standing watch.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_12: I serve the court, the capital, and the sovereign. In all three directions at once, most days.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_13: The Commander wants the west path watched. So I am watching it.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_14: People ask about bravery more often than they ask whether the road is safe.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_15: If someone says they are allowed through the Capital gates, send them to me first.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_16: A quiet road is still a road worth guarding. That's most of what I do here in {capital_name}.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_17: I do not mind rain on watch. I mind people complaining to me in it.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_18: If the royal guard passes, give them room.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_19: Remember this lesson: a blade is useful, but judgment keeps more people alive than iron.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_20: Stay behind the line if there is trouble. And no, the line is not a suggestion.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_21: A knight without discipline isn't a knight. That's the first thing you learn when you earn the title.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_22: People who have never stood a night watch don't quite understand what the knightly order does. I don't resent that. Much.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_24: A good guard learns which warnings are real and which fools are loud.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_25: I would rather earn respect than be given it. The title is given. The respect I work for daily.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_knight_26: If {capital_name} sleeps peacefully, that is enough praise for me.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_lord_comm: The royal household has {royal_household_count} members now. As Lord Commander, I try to know all of them by name.
I have seen {capital_name} change more than once. I'm sure soon enough I will see it change again.
The military of {capital_name} is my responsibility. I have found that people complain about discipline until disorder reaches their doorstep.
A Commander who is not feared at least a little is not doing their job correctly.
Every guard in this capital is an extension of my word. And I chose my words very carefully.
{capital_name} may have had commanders before me, but I intend to be the one they compare future commanders to.
My role in a coup attempt is not something I take lightly. Do let me know if you hear anything.
The hardest part of command is making people prepare for trouble they cannot see.
People who have never stood a night watch don't quite understand what the knightly order does. I don't resent that. Much.
I would rather earn respect than be given it. The title is given. The respect I work for daily.
Command is not given. It is maintained every single day.
A capital without military leadership is a capital that doesn't know how fragile it is.
I have held this position through quiet periods and through raids. Neither is as simple as it looks from the outside.
My standard for the guard is high. I know it. They know it. We've found an understanding.
Lord Commander is a title that carries history with it. I will do my duty with its due diligence.
A good commander is not always a visible one and a guard who wants glory usually needs more training. Remember that if you ever want to be a Knight.
When the capital is at risk, the Sovereign looks to me. I have no interest in disappointing them.
Tell the east guard I want the post changed before dusk.
A Commander who does not know the names of their guards is not a Commander. They are a title.
The military of {capital_name} reflects the court. When the court is steady, the guard is steady.
Do not crowd the gate. It makes everyone slower.
I want the archers where they can see, not where they look impressive.
No one stands alone when a Pillager approaches. Make sure they know that.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_lord_or_l: The master professionals of {capital_name} are the foundation of this court. I came from among them.
People bring me concerns that they won't bring to the higher nobility. I consider it privilege.
Lords and ladies sit between the court and the commons. It is a useful place, but is also a complicated one. Do let me know if there is anything I can assist with in those manners.
There are titles higher than mine. There are also responsibilities greater than mine but I do not envy them.
{sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} can rely on the lords and ladies of this court. I intend to make sure that is true.
A lordship is an entry into the politics of this court. I stepped into it with eyes wide open.
People I've known for years now address me differently. It is strange to get used to.
There is real work in this role, more than people outside the court realize.
I remember what this capital was before it had titles. Some days that perspective is more useful than any rank.
If this is a complaint, speak plainly. I hear enough polished nonsense.
I was easier to find before I had a title.
Bring the matter to me before bringing it to the Hand, I'll see what I can do for you.
Half of being noble is knowing when to stop talking.
The court has been busy today. I am pleased to have avoided most of it with skill.
Here's a tip for you if you ever want to survive this court. If you need a witness, ask before the argument starts.
A title gets you into the room, but does not make the room pleasant. If you intend to join the noble ranks of {capital_name} you should understand that.
I serve {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} and I serve {capital_name}. When those two things conflict, I try to find the version that does not.
Being amongst the lords of {capital_name} is mostly being the person willing to answer questions that nobody else claimed.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_duke_or_d: {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} bestowed this rank upon me. I serve it by making their court stronger.
Ducal rank comes with expectation. The petition was only the beginning of my service to {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name}.
A duchy sounds grand until everyone expects you to solve disputes older than their grandparents.
The latest development in {capital_name} — {latest_event} — has implications for the nobility that most haven't thought through yet.
People ask how I got here. Hard work, patience, and a sovereign who was watching.
Lords and knights look to the dukes and duchesses of {capital_name} for signals. I try to make sure the signals I send are worth following.
My responsibility is to {capital_name}. The title is just the shape that responsibility takes.
Some who hold this rank rest on it. I have never understood that, {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} elevated me for a reason.
Being elevated changes how people see you, but does not change who you are. That part is still your choice.
I have more standing in this court than I ever expected to reach. It comes with more to answer for.
I advise. I support. I serve. The title makes that sound grander than it sometimes feels.
If the lords are gathering, someone should ask why before they decide.
No, I am not bringing that to the sovereign yet.
I heard the petition. I did not hear a plan.
Tell the new lord to stop bowing at me in doorways.
If the court wants my answer today, it should have asked yesterday.
I will attend the hall when the hall stops attracting fools.
A duchy comes with many visitors. Few are welcome.
If it concerns my standing, say so. We can both save time.
A Duke who forgets that they serve the capital and not the other way around is a problem waiting to happen.
Do people imagine ducal rank comes with quiet mornings? I have not found one yet.
I spend more time weighing other people’s quarrels than enjoying my own comfort.
Have you ever noticed how quickly respect becomes expectation?
People bring me disputes with one side missing and expect wisdom by sunset.
A duchy teaches you which families forgive slowly and which never intended to.
A noble house can survive many things, but careless pride is costly.
{hand_title} {hand_name} hears the complaints first, but nobles feel them soon enough.
A noble house in {capital_name} rises fastest when it remembers the people below it.
{capital_name} has enough pride already; it needs nobles who can be useful.
A Duke or Duchess must learn which quarrels deserve attention and which only want an audience.
Influence feels grand until it becomes someone else’s burden placed in your hands, understand that if you ever want to be amongst us.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_01: {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} carries more than people realize. It is my duty as heir that I try to make sure some of that weight is shared.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_02: The court sees me as an extension of {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name}. I try to be worthy of that association.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_03: I have no sceptre, no petition rights, no formal power of decree. And yet {capital_name} is different because I am here.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_04: Everything I do in {capital_name} is watched. I had to stop pretending otherwise a long time ago.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_05: Do people see the heir clearly, or only the Crown waiting behind them?
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_06: I wish the court would understand that the future is easier for others to discuss than for one person to carry.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_07: I am {heir_title}, heir to the Throne of {capital_name}. What comes after that is not up to me to decide alone.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_08: If this is about succession, I would rather talk about literally anything else.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_09: If they are looking for me, tell them I am definitely not hiding.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_10: People speak of duty more easily when it belongs to someone else.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_11: I know where I stand in the line to the Throne. Everyone keeps reminding me.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_12: {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} always tells me that as an heir of {capital_name}, I must learn the people before I can inherit their loyalty.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_13: If the {sovereign_title} asks, I was in training with the Knights earlier today.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_14: I do not need another lesson on posture today.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_15: There are {royal_child_count} of us in the royal line. I am simply the one who is next.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_16: People ask me what kind of ruler I will be. I think the honest answer is: I do not know yet. I hope a good one.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_17: Sometimes I worry about the stories they will tell of me when I'm gone.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_18: {capital_name} will change between now and when I rule. I try to prepare for a future I cannot fully see.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_19: I try not to think too much about what inheriting the throne actually means. Then I think about it anyway.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_20: An heir is a promise the dynasty makes to the future. I try to be a promise worth keeping.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_21: I asked an old advisor once what the hardest part of ruling was. She told me: making decisions when you're not sure. Not the most helpful thing she could have said.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_22: Some heirs spend their whole life waiting. I would rather spend mine learning.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_23: The court sees the title. I hope, eventually, they also see the person.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_24: Succession is a line drawn in ink. It feels much more fragile than that.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_25: If I inherit this capital, I want to have earned it before I ever sit in the seat.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_26: Are families speaking well of the Crown, or only speaking carefully?
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_27: Have you heard what ordinary residents are complaining about most?
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_28: Everyone has advice for me now, even people who barely know how to manage their own household.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_29: One day, {capital_name} may expect more from me than I know how to give yet.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_30: I try to watch how {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} carries the Crown when no one is praising it.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_31: {hand_title} {hand_name} sees the troubles before most of us do, and for that I'm grateful.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_32: I wonder what {capital_name} will remember about these years when I am older.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_heir_33: When people speak of {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name}, I listen for what they are afraid to say plainly.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_royal_chi: People sometimes forget the consort has ears. That is their mistake.
I am a child of {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name}. That is a fact that shapes every room I walk into.
The heir is {heir_name}. I have made peace with that. Mostly.
Growing up in a royal household means learning that politics is just family with higher stakes.
{capital_name} is my home. Not just my birthplace — my home. I intend to serve it.
If the tutor asks, you have not seen me.
The guards never answer the interesting questions.
I know where the old stairs go and I'm not telling.
Adults speak of the future like children are not the ones expected to live in it.
If I am late, blame the Maester. The book was heavy.
I asked why people bow. Everyone gave a different answer.
The throne room is colder than it looks.
The dynasty is only as strong as the people in it.
I know the succession order. I know where I stand in it. I choose not to think about it too often.
If I inherit this capital, I want to have earned it before I ever sit the Throne.
There are more of us than people remember. The court has a lot of names to keep straight.
I was born into a title, but I'd like to think I'm building something beyond it.
If I've learned anything it is that the smallest person in a royal family can still make the whole room careful.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_sovereign: Every decision I make in {capital_name} will be written into the chronicle eventually.
{heir_name} is my named heir. Spread the word, I want no confusion when the time comes.
{commander_name} keeps the court safe. I trust that completely, and I say it publicly because trust should not be assumed.
The court reflects the sovereign. If {capital_name} is uneasy, I am asking myself why.
I have {royal_child_count} children. Each of them will be prepared for whatever role the dynasty asks of them.
{capital_name} did not always have a sovereign. The people who built it without one deserve to be remembered.
People are not sure how to speak to me now. I understand. I am not sure either, sometimes.
A crown is not something you put on. It is something you grow into. I am still growing.
The court reflects the sovereign. When I am uncertain, I can feel it spread outward.
Every decision I make here will outlast the moment I make it. I try to remember that.
My heir knows the weight they will carry. I have been honest with them about it.
I did not expect the loneliness of it. That is the part nobody tells you.
I hold this throne by choice. That means I hold it by responsibility too.
If this is urgent, start with the part where it became urgent.
Tell the Hand I have seen the petition. No, not that one. The other one.
The Commander wants more guards at the gate. I am inclined to agree.
If the herald is looking for me, ask whether they need me or only my title.
If the heir is missing, check the Maester first. Then the stables.
The chronicle can wait until after the decision is made.
I will hear the matter in the hall. Not in the doorway.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_01: If it begins with ‘small matter,’ it is never a small matter.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_02: Someone brought me a petition with soup on it so today, I am choosing patience.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_03: {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} wants this settled before nightfall. Naturally, everyone waited until the afternoon to inform me.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_04: My title is {hand_title}. Most days that means being interrupted by people who say they are sorry.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_05: No, that does not need to reach {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name}. Not yet.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_06: If the sovereign has already answered, why is this on my desk?
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_07: I need three names, one witness, and fewer opinions.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_08: Tell the herald I approved the short version.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_09: If this matter can wait, prove it by leaving.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_10: No, I am not taking that to the sovereign during supper.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_11: The court is not confused. The court is avoiding being clear.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_12: Walk with me. I can listen or stand still, not both.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_13: I need {commander_name}, two witnesses, and a room with fewer people in it.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_15: If the sovereign asks, I handled it. If anyone else asks, I am handling it.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_16: You need the sovereign? Try the hall first. If they are not there, try wherever the trouble is.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_17: I can speak with you, but not for long. People start lining up if I stand still.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_18: If this is about a petition, leave it on the desk. If it is urgent, tell me why before I decide it is not.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_19: The title sounds grand, yes. Mostly, it means people find me when they do not know who else to bother.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_20: No, the sovereign has not ignored your request. I am the delay, apparently.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_21: If you see the herald, tell them I have not forgotten. I am avoiding them with purpose.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_22: I liked this job better before I understood it.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_23: Walk with me if you need something. I am late to three places today already.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_24: {capital_name} has {capital_population} people now, and somehow every complaint still fits on my desk.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_hand_25: The royal household has {royal_household_count} people in it. That is not a household; that is a second court.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_grand_mae: The chronicle is not a coaster. I have said this more than once today already.
I asked for quiet, not a procession.
That book is older than your title. Hold it properly.
I can advise {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name}. I cannot make them listen.
The royal household has {royal_household_count} people. That is a great many headaches.
If you are here about a cough, sit down. If you are here about court business, sit down farther away from me.
People ask for my advice and then look offended when it is advice. If they do not want to treat their wound the way I say to, they can come back when they lose it.
No, I do not know whether your dream meant anything. Eat something and sleep properly tonight.
If you are bleeding, sit. If you are complaining, stand over there and wait.
I need ink, quiet, and someone to stop opening that door.
The chronicle is there to tell the story of what happened. Not what people wish had happened.
The chronicle is not missing. It is exactly where careless people do not look.
If the child swallowed something, start with what.
dialogue.mcacapitals_chat_rank_royal_con: I married {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name}. I did not marry every argument in {capital_name}, though some days it feels close.
When {sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} says they are fine, I usually start asking better questions.
Some days I miss being addressed by my name before my title.
The royal children are easier to manage than the courtiers. At least children admit when they want something.
If you need a favour, start honestly. I get enough polished nonsense in the hall.
The guard at the door has been standing there all morning. I hope someone remembered to feed them.
The nursery is louder than the council chamber today. Better arguments, too.
If this is about the sovereign, ask clearly. I have had enough careful questions for one morning.
{sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} missed breakfast again. If {hand_name} asks, I tried.
The royal children have been running through {capital_name} like the guards are obstacles.
{sovereign_title} {sovereign_name} has been in the hall all morning. Send food before sending more questions.
If this is about {latest_event}, ask plainly. Everyone keeps circling it like a nervous chicken.
Have you seen the sovereign? They were supposed to be in the hall.
If you see the Hand, tell them I am not ignoring them. Not on purpose.
